You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 6ded286555c2518be2f2d438f83dfaba3f0100fd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ben Hutchings <ben.hutchings@codethink.co.uk>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2015 00:52:08 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] sh_eth: Fix RX recovery on R-Car in case of RX ring underrun

In case of RX ring underrun (RDE), we attempt to reset the software
descriptor pointers (dirty_rx and cur_rx) to match where the hardware
will read the next descriptor from, as that might not be the first
dirty descriptor.  This relies on reading RDFAR, but that register
doesn't exist on all supported chips - specifically, not on the R-Car
chips.  This will result in unpredictable behaviour on those chips
after an RDE.

Make this pointer reset conditional and assume that it isn't needed on
the R-Car chips.  This fix also assumes that RDFAR is never exposed at
offset 0 in the memory map - this is currently true, and a subsequent
commit will fix the ambiguity between offset 0 and no-offset in the
register offset maps.

Fixes: 79fba9f51755 ("net: sh_eth: fix the rxdesc pointer when rx ...")
Signed-off-by: Ben Hutchings <ben.hutchings@codethink.co.uk>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/renesas/sh_eth.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/renesas/sh_eth.c
index 5c212a833bcf..3309494d12ad 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/renesas/sh_eth.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/renesas/sh_eth.c
@@ -1543,7 +1543,7 @@ static int sh_eth_rx(struct net_device *ndev, u32 intr_status, int *quota)
 	/* If we don't need to check status, don't. -KDU */
 	if (!(sh_eth_read(ndev, EDRRR) & EDRRR_R)) {
 		/* fix the values for the next receiving if RDE is set */
-		if (intr_status & EESR_RDE) {
+		if (intr_status & EESR_RDE && mdp->reg_offset[RDFAR] != 0) {
 			u32 count = (sh_eth_read(ndev, RDFAR) -
 				     sh_eth_read(ndev, RDLAR)) >> 4;
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/net/ethernet/renesas/sh_eth.c`**
- The condition for resetting the software descriptor pointers (`dirty_rx` and `cur_rx`) during a receive ring underrun (RDE) has been modified. 
- The original line:
  ```c
  if (intr_status & EESR_RDE) {
  ```
  has been changed to:
  ```c
  if (intr_status & EESR_RDE && mdp->reg_offset[RDFAR] != 0) {
  ```
- This change ensures that the reset of the pointers only occurs if the `RDFAR` register is present (i.e., its offset is not zero), which is a specific consideration for the R-Car chips that do not have the `RDFAR` register.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in the `sh_eth.c` file addresses a bug related to RX ring underrun handling specifically for R-Car chips. By making the pointer reset conditional on the existence of the `RDFAR` register, the patch prevents unpredictable behavior that could arise from attempting to access a non-existent register on these chips.
- This change is a direct response to the issues highlighted in the previous commit referenced in the patch (`Fixes: 79fba9f51755`), which aimed to fix the RX descriptor pointer handling but did not account for the absence of the `RDFAR` register on certain hardware. The new condition ensures that the fix is applicable only to supported hardware configurations, thereby enhancing stability and reliability.
